security_audit.summary: Eighty-four of 85 static findings are false positives caused by documentation syntax, scientific terms, fixed output examples, or expected Forge API references. One shortened community link is a low-risk redirect concern, and the protein generation workflows create a separate medium-severity dual-use biosafety risk.

remediation.issue: Function-conditioned protein generation can be misused for harmful biological design.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit refusal and screening guidance for harmful functions, plus expert biosafety review before synthesis or experimental validation.

remediation.issue: The community resource uses a shortened URL that hides its final destination.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the shortened Slack link with a canonical destination on a trusted domain.

content.user_title: Design and Analyze Proteins with ESM
content.value_statement: Protein modeling workflows often require unfamiliar ESM APIs, model choices, and generation settings. This skill provides practical guidance for local ESM models and scalable Forge inference.
actual_capabilities: Guides masked protein sequence generation with local ESM3 models or the Forge API.
Explains structure prediction and inverse folding with ESMProtein and generation tracks.
Shows ESM C embedding extraction for similarity, clustering, classification, and transfer learning.
Covers function-conditioned generation and iterative sequence, structure, and function refinement.
Provides batch processing, retry, checkpoint, cache, and model selection patterns for Forge workloads.
limitations: Large local models require substantial memory, compatible hardware, and downloaded model weights.
Forge workflows require network access, a valid API token, and compliance with service limits and costs.
Generated proteins require independent computational review, biosafety screening, and experimental validation.
Reference examples may need updates for the installed ESM package version and local environment.

use_cases.title: Explore protein representations
use_cases.description: Generate ESM C embeddings and plan similarity, clustering, or classification analyses for a sequence collection.

use_cases.title: Prototype protein designs
use_cases.description: Plan sequence completion, inverse folding, or function-conditioned ESM3 experiments with clear validation stages.

use_cases.title: Scale inference pipelines
use_cases.description: Design Forge workflows with asynchronous batches, retries, checkpoints, caching, and rate-limit controls.

prompt_templates.title: Generate one embedding
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to generate one ESM C embedding for [protein sequence]. Recommend a model, pooling strategy, device, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Predict a protein structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a structure-prediction workflow for [sequence] using [local ESM3 or Forge]. Include model choice, generation settings, PDB output, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan inverse folding
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an inverse-folding experiment for [PDB file]. Explain sequence masking, sampling settings, candidate ranking, structural checks, and biosafety review.

prompt_templates.title: Build a scalable Forge pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Forge pipeline for [dataset] and [task]. Include batching, retries, checkpointing, caching, cost controls, data handling, and biosafety review gates.

output_examples.input: Recommend an ESM C workflow for clustering 2,000 protein sequences.
output: Model: start with ESM C 300M for throughput, then compare a larger model on a representative subset.
Processing: group similar lengths, batch on the available device, and cache pooled embeddings.
Analysis: normalize embeddings, cluster them, inspect representatives, and save assignments with reproducible parameters.

output_examples.input: Plan structure prediction for a single enzyme sequence.
output_examples.output: Use ESM3 with the structure track, record model and sampling settings, export a PDB, and assess confidence before experimental use.

output_examples.input: Outline a reliable Forge batch generation job.
output: Submit bounded asynchronous batches and apply exponential backoff for rate limits.
Checkpoint completed items, cache deterministic results, and record failed requests for review.
Review provider data terms and apply biosafety screening before downstream synthesis or testing.

best_practices: Prototype with smaller models, then compare larger models only when quality gains justify added cost.
Record model identifiers, generation parameters, seeds, input provenance, and validation results.
Screen generated sequences for biosafety concerns and require expert review before experimental validation.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated sequences, structures, or function labels as experimentally validated results.
Do not place Forge tokens in source files, prompts, notebooks, or shared logs.
Do not send sensitive sequences to remote services without reviewing access controls and provider terms.

faq.question: Which ESM model families does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers ESM3 for generation and structure tasks, plus ESM C for embeddings and representation learning.

faq.question: Does the skill run models automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and examples that users adapt and execute in their own environment.

faq.question: Is a Forge API token required?
faq.answer: A token is required only for Forge workflows. Local open-model workflows do not use Forge credentials.

faq.question: Do local workflows require a GPU?
faq.answer: Hardware needs depend on model size and sequence length. Larger models commonly need substantial accelerator memory.

faq.question: Are generated proteins ready for laboratory use?
faq.answer: No. They require independent validation, biosafety screening, expert review, and appropriate experimental controls.

faq.question: How should sensitive protein data be handled?
faq.answer: Prefer approved local processing or review Forge access controls, retention terms, and organizational policies before transmission.
